title: Spherical collapse and cluster number counts in DHOST theories that pass the constraints from gravitational waves
comment: 23 pages, 4 figures
summary:
We investigate the spherical collapse model and the abundance of galaxy clusters in a class of degenerate higher-order scalar--tensor (DHOST) theories in which gravitational waves do not decay into scalar perturbations and which are consistent with current constraints from gravitational-wave observations. We find that deviations from Einstein gravity can become significant at late times when the background universe is close to the scaling regime during the matter-dominated epoch. These deviations suppress the growth of linear matter perturbations on small scales while increasing the extrapolated linear density contrast at collapse, obtained from the spherical collapse model. Using the analytic mass function, we compute the corresponding cluster number counts. The minimum mass threshold in the mass integration for each redshift bin is determined by matching the predicted number counts in the $Λ$CDM model with those inferred from the eROSITA survey. We find that the cluster abundance reaches its maximum at low redshift bin, and that the number of clusters in the highest redshift bin is suppressed as the deviation from Einstein gravity becomes larger. The parameters of the theory are chosen such that the deviation from Einstein gravity at present is consistent with the local astrophysical bounds from binary pulsar observations. We find that even under such strict constraints, the upper bound on the deviation leads to lower predicted number counts compared with the $Λ$CDM model emulating the eROSITA survey results.
  However, this may be a consequence of the uncertainties in computing the number counts for the DHOST theories using the spherical collapse model and the analytical mass function.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates the spherical collapse model and galaxy cluster abundance in DHOST theories consistent with gravitational-wave constraints. Deviations from Einstein gravity suppress linear matter perturbations on small scales but increase the linear density contrast at collapse. Cluster number counts are computed using the analytic mass function, and results show that even under strict astrophysical bounds, the predicted counts are lower than ΛCDM, though this may be due to modeling uncertainties.
AI.motivation: To understand how degenerate higher-order scalar-tensor (DHOST) theories—a class of modified gravity consistent with gravitational-wave observations—affect the spherical collapse model and galaxy cluster abundance, and to assess whether such theories can be distinguished from ΛCDM using cluster counts from surveys like eROSITA.
AI.method: The authors study the spherical collapse model in DHOST theories where gravitational waves do not decay into scalar perturbations. They compute the linear density contrast at collapse, use the analytic mass function to calculate cluster number counts, and determine the minimum mass threshold per redshift bin by matching ΛCDM predictions to eROSITA survey data. Theory parameters are constrained using binary pulsar observations.
AI.result: Deviations from Einstein gravity become significant at late times near the scaling regime in matter domination. These deviations suppress small-scale linear matter perturbations while increasing the extrapolated linear density contrast at collapse. Cluster abundance peaks at low redshift; higher redshift bins show suppressed counts as deviations grow. Even under strict binary pulsar bounds, the upper deviation limit yields lower predicted number counts than ΛCDM emulating eROSITA results.
AI.conclusion: DHOST theories consistent with gravitational-wave and binary pulsar constraints predict lower galaxy cluster number counts than ΛCDM, particularly at high redshifts. However, this conclusion may be affected by uncertainties in applying the spherical collapse model and analytic mass function to these theories.

title: Improved recipes for peculiar velocity power spectra using Evolution Mapping
comment: 11 pages plus one appendix, comments are welcome
summary: We present new fitting functions for the velocity divergence auto- and cross-power spectra, $P_{θθ}(k)$ and $P_{δθ}(k)$, calibrated on gravity-only $N$-body simulations. By applying the Evolution Mapping framework, we revise existing prescriptions to introduce a physically motivated parametrisation in terms of the clustering amplitude $σ_{12}$, the RMS density fluctuation smoothed at $12\,\text{Mpc}$. This approach improves robustness and extends the range of applicability beyond that of previous models. Our fits are calibrated using a suite of multi-resolution simulations, with numerical convergence carefully quantified and sampling artefacts mitigated through a conservative patching strategy. This yields converged measurements up to $k\simeq0.56\,\mathrm{Mpc}^{-1}$ and percent-level accuracy for both $P_{θθ}(k)$ and $P_{δθ}(k)$ over a wide range of $σ_{12}$. Validation against independent simulations spanning a broad range of cosmological models confirms an accuracy of $1$-$2$ per cent on scales where the measurements are robust, systematically outperforming existing prescriptions. We further assess the impact of deviations from the exact evolution mapping relation induced by differing growth histories. For most cosmologies of practical interest, we find that neglecting these effects introduces only subdominant errors. We show that expressing fitting functions in $h$-dependent units leads to spurious, unphysical dependencies on the Hubble parameter, even for models with identical linear clustering. This provides strong empirical support for parametrising non-linear evolution in terms of $σ_{12}$ rather than $σ_{8}$. Our fitting functions provide a robust description of velocity power spectra, with direct applications to redshift-space distortion modelling in galaxy redshift surveys.

AI.tldr: New fitting functions for velocity divergence power spectra Pθθ(k) and Pδθ(k) are presented, calibrated on N-body simulations using the Evolution Mapping framework with σ12 parametrization, achieving percent-level accuracy up to k≃0.56 Mpc⁻¹ and outperforming existing models.
AI.motivation: To improve robustness and extend the range of applicability of velocity divergence power spectrum fitting functions beyond existing models, and to demonstrate that parametrizing non-linear evolution in terms of σ12 (rather than σ8) avoids spurious Hubble parameter dependencies.
AI.method: Applied the Evolution Mapping framework to revise existing prescriptions; calibrated fits using multi-resolution N-body simulations with quantified numerical convergence and a conservative patching strategy to mitigate sampling artefacts; validated against independent simulations across a broad range of cosmological models.
AI.result: Converged measurements up to k≃0.56 Mpc⁻¹ with percent-level accuracy for both Pθθ(k) and Pδθ(k) over a wide σ12 range; validation shows 1-2% accuracy, systematically outperforming existing prescriptions; showing that h-dependent units introduce spurious dependencies on the Hubble parameter.
AI.conclusion: The fitting functions provide a robust description of velocity power spectra with direct applications to redshift-space distortion modelling in galaxy redshift surveys, with strong empirical support for parametrising non-linear evolution in terms of σ12 rather than σ8.

title: The Magnetic Origin of Primordial Black Holes: Ultralight PBHs and Secondary GWs
comment: 33 pages, 11 figures. Comments and suggestions are heartily welcome
summary: Ultralight primordial black holes (PBHs) provide a compelling window into early-Universe cosmology. Following our earlier work, we explore a mechanism for the formation of ultralight PBHs sourced by primordial inflationary magnetic fields, without invoking an ultra-slow-roll phase of inflation. We propose a magnetogenesis model in which large curvature perturbations are induced at small scales, leading to the efficient production of ultralight PBHs across a broad mass spectrum. We analyze the phenomenological implications of these ultralight PBHs for early-Universe cosmology, particularly during reheating. We compute the resulting stochastic gravitational wave (GW) background generated by both the electromagnetic spectrum and evaporating PBHs, which exhibits distinctive features tied to the underlying magnetogenesis model parameters. Our results demonstrate that inflationary magnetic fields can serve as a viable and testable origin for ultralight PBHs, opening new avenues for probing the interplay between inflation, magnetogenesis, PBHs, and primordial gravitational waves.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a mechanism for forming ultralight primordial black holes (PBHs) using inflationary magnetic fields, bypassing the need for an ultra-slow-roll inflation phase. It computes the resulting stochastic gravitational wave background from both electromagnetic sources and evaporating PBHs, showing that inflationary magnetic fields offer a testable origin for ultralight PBHs, linking inflation, magnetogenesis, PBHs, and primordial gravitational waves.
AI.motivation: To explore a new mechanism for forming ultralight PBHs using primordial inflationary magnetic fields, avoiding the standard ultra-slow-roll inflation scenario, and to provide testable phenomenological signatures linking magnetogenesis, PBHs, and gravitational waves.
AI.method: The authors propose a magnetogenesis model where large curvature perturbations at small scales are induced by inflationary magnetic fields, leading to PBH formation. They then compute the stochastic gravitational wave background from both the electromagnetic spectrum and evaporating PBHs, analyzing its dependence on model parameters.
AI.result: Inflationary magnetic fields can efficiently produce ultralight PBHs across a broad mass spectrum, and the resulting stochastic gravitational wave background exhibits distinctive features tied to the magnetogenesis model parameters.
AI.conclusion: Inflationary magnetic fields are a viable, testable origin for ultralight PBHs, opening new avenues for probing the interplay between inflation, magnetogenesis, PBHs, and primordial gravitational waves.

title: The Hunt for Red Dual AGNs I: Spatially-Resolved Mid-IR Dual AGNs in the DeCam Legacy Survey
comment: 35 pages, including 5 tables, 10 figures, and 4 appendix sections. Submitted to ApJ; feedback welcome!
summary: Theoretical studies predict that dual AGNs are a critical stage of galaxy merger-driven supermassive black hole growth. Systematic searches for dual AGNs typically target late-stage mergers ($\leq10$ kpc nuclear separations) and select AGNs based on optical diagnostics. Yet, simulations predict that obscuration can occur early in the merger sequence, and that a significant fraction of dual AGNs can be found beyond $10$ kpc. Here, we report on a new sample of 157 spatially resolved mid-IR dual AGNs candidates selected based upon their mid-IR $W1-W2$ colors from the Wide-Field Infrared Survey Explorer and optically classified as galaxy merger candidates using imaging from the Dark Energy Camera Legacy Survey. Spectroscopic results are presented for approximately 2/3 of the sample. 76 candidates have been confirmed to reside in galaxy mergers; among these, 13 have been confirmed as bona fide mid-IR dual AGNs, while 63 represent strong dual AGN candidates that require further examination. 46 candidates have been rejected as non-merger contaminants (foreground-background AGNs, separations inconsistent with interacting galaxies, etc.). 35 candidates still await spectroscopic coverage. The confirmed and high confidence dual AGN candidates exhibit separations of 14.5-129 kpc; $>50$% reside at separations $>50$ kpc. Confirmed and high confidence candidates also exhibit a diversity of nuclear optical BPT classes. Seyfert-Seyferts and Seyfert-HIIs dominate the overall BPT pairs sample. 31% of confirmed mid-IR dual AGNs reside in multi-mergers involving three or more galaxies. The diversity in AGN properties and environments identified in this work highlights the importance of multiwavelength selection strategies and analyses in the quest to holistically understand dual AGNs as a population.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a new sample of 157 mid-IR dual AGN candidates selected via WISE W1-W2 colors and DECam imaging, with 76 confirmed in mergers, 13 confirmed as bona fide dual AGNs, and 63 as strong candidates. The sample shows separations of 14.5–129 kpc (>50% >50 kpc), diverse BPT classifications, and 31% in multi-mergers, highlighting the need for multiwavelength selection.
AI.motivation: Theoretical predictions suggest dual AGNs are a critical stage in galaxy merger-driven supermassive black hole growth, but systematic searches typically focus on late-stage mergers (≤10 kpc) and optical diagnostics, potentially missing obscured or widely separated (>10 kpc) dual AGNs predicted by simulations.
AI.method: Mid-IR dual AGN candidates were selected using WISE W1-W2 colors and optically classified as galaxy merger candidates from Dark Energy Camera Legacy Survey imaging. Spectroscopic follow-up was obtained for ~2/3 of the sample to confirm mergers and AGN activity.
AI.result: 157 candidates identified; 76 confirmed in mergers (13 bona fide dual AGNs, 63 strong candidates); 46 rejected as non-merger contaminants; 35 pending. Confirmed candidates show separations 14.5–129 kpc (>50% >50 kpc), diverse BPT classes (Seyfert-Seyfert and Seyfert-HII dominant), and 31% reside in multi-mergers.
AI.conclusion: The diversity in AGN properties and environments underscores the importance of multiwavelength selection strategies for a holistic understanding of the dual AGN population, particularly to capture widely separated and obscured systems missed by traditional optical-only searches.

title: Single field matter bounce with dark energy era: comparison with CMB Planck 2018 data and best fit parameters
comment: 12 pages, 6 figures
summary: In this work, we perform Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) analyses using the Planck 2018 cosmic microwave background (CMB) datasets, including temperature, polarization, and lensing, in order to compare matter bounce models with observational data. The particular model we considered contains a scalar field with an exponential potential, which behaves as dust in the asymptotic past of the contracting phase, it realizes a quantum bounce, and then behaves as a transient dark energy field at large scales in the expanding phase. The parameter $λ$ appearing in the exponential potential is directly related to the model's scalar spectral index, $n_s$, which is set free in the MCMC analyses, as well as the deepness of the bounce, which controls the amplitude of the power spectrum. We provide constraints on the cosmological parameters and compare the model's performance against the standard inflationary $Λ$CDM scenario. Our results indicate that Planck data alone cannot favor one model with respect to the other, showing that the model we investigate can be a viable alternative to inflation.

AI.tldr: The paper uses Planck 2018 CMB data to constrain a matter bounce model with an exponential scalar field potential, finding it cannot be statistically distinguished from standard inflationary ΛCDM, thus presenting a viable alternative to inflation.
AI.motivation: To test whether matter bounce models, which serve as alternatives to cosmic inflation, can be consistent with high-precision CMB observations from Planck 2018, and to determine if observational data can distinguish between bounce and inflation scenarios.
AI.method: Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) analyses applied to Planck 2018 CMB datasets (temperature, polarization, and lensing). The matter bounce model features a scalar field with exponential potential (parameter λ controlling spectral index n_s and bounce depth). Model performance is compared against standard inflationary ΛCDM.
AI.result: Planck data alone cannot statistically favor either the matter bounce model or the standard inflationary ΛCDM scenario. The constraints on cosmological parameters are provided, and the model's performance is comparable to inflation.
AI.conclusion: The matter bounce model investigated is a viable alternative to inflation, as current CMB data cannot distinguish between the two scenarios.

title: Massive Galaxies Form Early and Gray: Stellar Assembly and Dust Attenuation at $\mathbf{z>3.5}$ from CAPERS
comment: 24 pages, 11 figures, submitted to ApJL
summary: The stellar mass assembly of massive galaxies in the first few billion years of cosmic history remains a central challenge in galaxy formation. Galaxies with $M_\star \gtrsim 10^{10}M_\odot$ observed at $z \gtrsim 4$ must grow rapidly under conditions of intense gas accretion, feedback, and dust production. Observationally, their star-formation histories (SFHs) have been poorly constrained due to degeneracies inherent to broadband photometry. The advent of JWST enables direct spectroscopic access to detailed continuum shapes and rest-frame optical diagnostics at high redshift, providing a critical opportunity to reconstruct formation timescales of massive early galaxies. Here, we investigate massive galaxies using joint spectro-photometric SED fitting of JWST/NIRSpec prism spectroscopy from the CANDELS-Area Prism Epoch of Reionization Survey (CAPERS). Our sample comprises 148 galaxies selected photometrically with log $(M_\star/M_\odot) > 9.5$ at $z > 3.5$. We find that the most massive galaxies (log $(M_\star/M_\odot) > 10.5$) preferentially exhibit shallow, gray dust attenuation curves, consistent with higher dust optical depths and large grain sizes. We also find significant diversity in the time at which galaxies form 25% of their stellar mass. While formation timescales converge toward later cosmic times, galaxies with lower sSFR ($\lesssim -9$) at the observation epoch formed significantly earlier than systems with higher sSFRs. Across the full mass range, inferred assembly times are systematically earlier than model predictions, suggesting more rapid early growth than currently captured theoretically. These results underscore the importance of spectroscopic constraints and flexible SFH and dust models for reconstructing high-redshift massive galaxy formation histories.

AI.tldr: Using JWST/NIRSpec prism spectroscopy from the CAPERS survey on 148 massive galaxies at z>3.5, the authors find that the most massive galaxies (log M/M☉ > 10.5) show shallow gray dust attenuation, diverse formation timescales, and systematically earlier assembly than model predictions, indicating more rapid early growth than current theories capture.
AI.motivation: Understanding the stellar mass assembly of massive galaxies in the early universe (z≳4) remains a central challenge, as their star-formation histories have been poorly constrained due to degeneracies in broadband photometry. JWST's spectroscopic capabilities now provide a critical opportunity to reconstruct formation timescales.
AI.method: Joint spectro-photometric SED fitting of JWST/NIRSpec prism spectroscopy from the CAPERS survey; 148 galaxies with log(M⋆/M⊙) > 9.5 at z > 3.5 were analyzed using flexible SFH and dust models.
AI.result: Most massive galaxies (log M/M☉ > 10.5) exhibit shallow gray dust attenuation curves (higher dust optical depths, large grain sizes). Significant diversity in 25% mass assembly timescales; lower sSFR galaxies formed earlier. Inferred assembly times are systematically earlier than model predictions across the full mass range.
AI.conclusion: Spectroscopic constraints from JWST, along with flexible SFH and dust models, are essential for reconstructing high-redshift massive galaxy formation histories. Current theoretical models may underestimate the rapidity of early massive galaxy growth.

title: KiDS+VIKING-450 cosmology with Bayesian hierarchical model redshift distributions
comment: Accepted for publication in MNRAS
summary: Tomographic redshift distributions from photometric data are crucial ingredients in cosmic shear analysis, since they are required for the theoretical calculation of the signal based on the redshift distribution of the galaxies where the shear field is sampled. In this paper, we develop as a proof of concept Leistedt et al.'s template-based Bayesian Hierarchical Model framework into an application to weak lensing data by sampling the redshift distributions of the galaxies in the KiDS+VIKING-450 survey. We also use a principal component analysis to provide a set of representative templates drawn from a large superset. For computational tractability, subsets of $10^5$ galaxies are chosen to determine the redshift distributions, and we test the sensitivity of the cosmological inference to the subset chosen, finding it to be subdominant compared to the statistical error. We marginalise over the inferred redshift distributions and find that the Bayesian method increases the clustering parameter compared with previous studies, alleviating the $S_8$ tension with Planck, where $S_{8}\equivσ_{8}\sqrt{Ω_{\tm{m}}/0.3}=0.756\pm 0.039$, assuming flat $Λ$CDM. The tension with Planck for this survey is reduced from $2.3σ$ to $1.9σ$. We also infer a value for the matter density, $Ω_{\tm{m}}=0.31\pm 0.10$.

AI.tldr: The paper applies a Bayesian Hierarchical Model to infer tomographic redshift distributions for weak lensing, using KiDS+VIKING-450 data with PCA-derived templates. The method reduces the S8 tension with Planck from 2.3σ to 1.9σ, yielding S8=0.756±0.039 and Ωm=0.31±0.10.
AI.motivation: Accurate tomographic redshift distributions from photometric data are essential for cosmic shear analysis, as they underpin theoretical signal calculations. Existing methods may not fully marginalise over uncertainties, motivating a Bayesian hierarchical approach.
AI.method: The authors extend Leistedt et al.'s template-based Bayesian Hierarchical Model to weak lensing data (KiDS+VIKING-450). PCA extracts representative templates from a large superset. Subsets of 10^5 galaxies are used for computational tractability, and sensitivity to subset choice is tested.
AI.result: Marginalising over inferred redshift distributions increases the clustering parameter, reducing the S8 tension with Planck from 2.3σ to 1.9σ. S8=0.756±0.039 and Ωm=0.31±0.10 under flat ΛCDM.
AI.conclusion: The Bayesian method alleviates the S8 tension, providing a more robust treatment of redshift distribution uncertainties in cosmic shear cosmology.

title: When galaxies burst: enhanced shot-noise for line-intensity mapping in the JWST era
comment: 6 pages, 5 figures (with appendices: 11 pages, 7 figures)
summary: Recent JWST observations indicate that star formation at $z\!\sim\!4-6$ is more stochastic than previously assumed, with rms log-SFR scatter $\sim\!0.6$ dex at $M_h\!\sim\!10^{11}M_{\odot}$, growing toward smaller halos and time-correlated on $\sim\!25$ Myr. This is significantly higher than the typical $\sim\!0.3$ dex phenomenological lognormal scatter assumed in standard line-intensity mapping (LIM) forecasts. We propagate the JWST-era burstiness through to the LIM shot-noise power spectrum and show that the result is a simple multiplicative correction: the deterministic shot noise multiplied by a line-dependent boost factor $B_λ$ derived in closed form by convolving the SFR correlation function with the stellar-population-synthesis kernel of each line. At $z\!\sim\!6$, we find $B_{{\rm H}α}\!\simeq\!7$ and $B\!\sim\!2.5$-$3.5$ for longer-window tracers ([CII], CO, UV) - factors of $\sim\!2$-$5$ above the standard prescription, and growing further toward higher redshift. The enhancement transforms the LIM landscape: it improves auto-spectrum detectability and suppresses lower-redshift interloper contamination, but degrades cosmological applications such as BAO that rely on a clean clustering measurement. Crucially, it also opens a new use of LIM as a diagnostic of high-redshift star-formation physics beyond the regime of individually resolved galaxies: redshift tomography of a single line constrains the amplitude and mass dependence of the burstiness, while cross-line shot-noise correlations probe its time coherence.

AI.tldr: JWST reveals that star formation at z~4-6 is much more bursty (stochastic) than previously assumed, with log-SFR scatter ~0.6 dex, and this burstiness boosts line-intensity mapping shot-noise power spectra by factors of ~2-7 (depending on line and redshift) relative to standard forecasts, transforming detectability, interloper contamination, and opening new diagnostics of high-redshift star-formation physics.
AI.motivation: JWST observations show that star formation at z~4-6 is far more stochastic (rms log-SFR scatter ~0.6 dex) than the ~0.3 dex lognormal scatter assumed in standard line-intensity mapping (LIM) forecasts, motivating the need to quantify the impact of this burstiness on LIM observables.
AI.method: The authors propagate the JWST-era burstiness through to the LIM shot-noise power spectrum by deriving a simple multiplicative correction: the deterministic shot noise multiplied by a line-dependent boost factor Bλ, obtained in closed form by convolving the SFR correlation function with the stellar-population-synthesis kernel of each line.
AI.result: At z~6, B_Hα ≃ 7 and B ~ 2.5-3.5 for longer-window tracers ([CII], CO, UV) — factors of ~2-5 above standard prescriptions, growing further toward higher redshift. The enhancement improves auto-spectrum detectability and suppresses interloper contamination, but degrades BAO and other clustering-based cosmological applications.
AI.conclusion: The burstiness transforms the LIM landscape and opens a new diagnostic: redshift tomography of a single line constrains the amplitude and mass dependence of burstiness, while cross-line shot-noise correlations probe its time coherence, enabling LIM to serve as a probe of high-redshift star-formation physics beyond individually resolved galaxies.

title: Strong Gravitational Lensing with the James Webb Space Telescope
comment: Invited review for \emph{Contemporary Physics}. Accepted for publication. 37 pages including references; 13 figures, including those adapted from the literature
summary: The theory of General Relativity predicts that, since massive bodies curve spacetime, light from a distant source would be deflected by a foreground massive object -- a phenomenon known as \emph{Gravitational Lensing}. Historically, the strength of deflection of light from background stars by the sun, during the 1919 solar eclipse, supplied one of the first proofs for the theory of General Relativity. However, it is only in the last few decades, with the advent of the Hubble Space Telescope and other large, ground-based facilities, that lensing has become a principal tool in modern astronomy. Lensing allows us to study both the matter content of the lensing bodies such as galaxies or clusters of galaxies, mainly dominated by the otherwise-invisible \emph{dark matter}, and the distant background sources that are being lensed by them. Strong gravitational lensing, where sources are substantially magnified and multiply imaged, is particularly useful to that end. The substantial magnification allows for a high-resolution view of the sources and to detect fainter and farther objects than would otherwise be possible; and image multiplicity helps in verifying the distance to them, and for studying variable or transient sources. Paired with the unprecedented capabilities of the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST), lensing now allows us to observe, detect, and study distant sources like never before. I summarise recent advances in strong-lensing applications and near-future prospects with JWST.

AI.tldr: This paper reviews strong gravitational lensing as a tool in modern astronomy, its historical roots in testing General Relativity, its applications for studying dark matter and distant sources, and recent advances and future prospects with the James Webb Space Telescope.
AI.motivation: To summarize the current state and near-future potential of strong gravitational lensing for studying dark matter in lensing bodies and magnifying distant background sources, particularly in the context of JWST's enhanced capabilities.
AI.method: A review summarizing recent advances in strong-lensing applications, including using source magnification and image multiplicity to study high-redshift, faint, and transient objects, combined with JWST observations.
AI.result: Strong gravitational lensing paired with JWST now enables the observation and study of distant sources at unprecedented depth and resolution, providing insights into dark matter distributions and extremely faint background objects.
AI.conclusion: JWST will dramatically advance strong-lensing science by enabling high-resolution studies of the most distant and faintest sources, shedding light on both the lensing mass distributions (dominated by dark matter) and the properties of lensed background galaxies.

title: Determining star formation histories and age-metallicity relations with convolutional neural networks
summary:
We aim to develop a state-of-the-art tool to infer detailed star formation histories (SFHs) and age-metallicity relations from realistic observational data, while mitigating classical degeneracies and substantially reducing computational cost. In particular, we seek to exploit the complementarity of spectroscopic and photometric data to improve constraints on the spatially resolved SFH and metallicity evolution of nearby galaxies in the PHANGS collaboration.
  We construct and train a convolutional neural network (CNN) that combines convolutional layers, attention mechanisms, and a shared latent space to jointly predict SFHs and metallicities in 16 age bins. The network simultaneously processes integral-field spectroscopic data from PHANGS-MUSE and five-band photometric fluxes from PHANGS-HST. Training is performed on a dataset of 165\,000 synthetic spectra and photometric measurements spanning a broad range of SFH shapes, metallicity evolution, dust attenuation, and signal-to-noise ratios representative of the observations.
  The CNN accurately recovers SFHs and age-metallicity relations over a wide range of evolutionary scenarios. The inferred luminosity- and mass-weighted mean ages and metallicities show negligible bias, with dispersions of $\sim0.12$ dex in age and $\sim0.03$ dex in metallicity. When applied to real PHANGS-MUSE and PHANGS-HST data for NGC\,3627, the network produces smooth, spatially coherent maps of stellar age and metallicity that recover physically meaningful structures, including younger populations tracing the spiral arms and star-forming regions. The CNN is approximately $5\times10^{3}$--$2\times10^{4}$ times faster than traditional full spectral fitting codes, providing a powerful and efficient alternative for the analysis of large spectro-photometric surveys.

AI.tldr: A CNN trained on synthetic spectra + photometry jointly predicts star formation histories and age-metallicity relations from PHANGS-MUSE and PHANGS-HST data, achieving ~0.12 dex age / ~0.03 dex metallicity precision while being 5×10³–2×10⁴ times faster than traditional spectral fitting.
AI.motivation: To develop a state-of-the-art tool that infers detailed SFHs and age-metallicity relations from realistic observations while mitigating classical degeneracies, reducing computational cost, and exploiting the complementarity of spectroscopic and photometric data for spatially resolved analysis of nearby galaxies in the PHANGS collaboration.
AI.method: A convolutional neural network combining convolutional layers, attention mechanisms, and a shared latent space to jointly predict SFHs and metallicities in 16 age bins. The network processes integral-field spectroscopic data (PHANGS-MUSE) and five-band photometric fluxes (PHANGS-HST). Training uses 165,000 synthetic spectra+photometry spanning diverse SFH shapes, metallicity evolution, dust attenuation, and S/N ratios.
AI.result: Accurate recovery of SFHs and age-metallicity relations; luminosity- and mass-weighted mean ages and metallicities show negligible bias with dispersions of ~0.12 dex (age) and ~0.03 dex (metallicity). Application to NGC 3627 yields smooth, spatially coherent maps where younger populations trace spiral arms and star-forming regions. The CNN is 5×10³–2×10⁴ times faster than traditional full spectral fitting codes.
AI.conclusion: The CNN provides a powerful, efficient alternative for large spectro-photometric surveys, enabling fast and accurate spatially resolved SFH and metallicity inference at a fraction of the computational cost of traditional methods.

title: Isocurvature-Free QCD Axion Dark Matter from Inflaton-Driven Early QCD: the Necessity of Inflationary Plateaus
comment: 9 pages, 2 figures
summary: A direct coupling between the inflaton and Standard Model gluons can dynamically raise the QCD confinement scale during inflation, making the axion temporarily heavy and suppressing axion isocurvature perturbations. As inflation proceeds, the confinement scale relaxes, the axion becomes light, and late-time de Sitter fluctuations can generate the observed dark matter abundance. We analyze this mechanism without specifying an inflationary potential, instead parametrizing the background by $ε(N) \propto 1/N^p$, where $N$ is the number of $e$-folds before the end of inflation. The single parameter $p$ distinguishes monomial models ($p=1$), standard plateau models ($p=2$), and ultra-flat plateau or hilltop-like models ($p\ge 3$). We (analytically) show that the mechanism selects plateau-like ($p\ge 2$) inflation: monomial models generically cause the confinement scale to grow too rapidly, while plateau models keep the QCD sector under perturbative control. In the minimal scenario, reheating occurs through the same inflaton-gluon coupling, and viable axion dark matter production is obtained when deconfinement occurs after the CMB window. The early-confinement sector also shifts the scalar spectral index to larger, bluer values, opening viable parameter space for models otherwise disfavored by CMB data.

AI.tldr: This paper shows that coupling the inflaton to Standard Model gluons can dynamically raise the QCD confinement scale during inflation, temporarily making the axion heavy and suppressing isocurvature perturbations, while later relaxation generates axion dark matter. The mechanism selects plateau-like inflation (p≥2) over monomial models and can shift the scalar spectral index to bluer values, opening new parameter space for CMB-favored models.
AI.motivation: The authors aim to address the problem of axion isocurvature perturbations, which are tightly constrained by CMB observations, by proposing a mechanism where the QCD confinement scale is dynamically raised during inflation to make the axion temporarily heavy, while still allowing it to later become light and generate the observed dark matter abundance.
AI.method: The mechanism is analyzed analytically without specifying an inflationary potential, instead parametrizing the background using ε(N) ∝ 1/N^p, where N is the number of e-folds before the end of inflation. The single parameter p distinguishes monomial models (p=1), standard plateau models (p=2), and ultra-flat plateau/hilltop models (p≥3). The analysis tracks the dynamical evolution of the QCD confinement scale and axion mass during inflation.
AI.result: The mechanism selects plateau-like (p≥2) inflation over monomial models. Monomial models (p=1) cause the confinement scale to grow too rapidly, while plateau models keep the QCD sector under perturbative control. Viable axion dark matter production is obtained when deconfinement occurs after the CMB window. The early-confinement sector also shifts the scalar spectral index to larger, bluer values.
AI.conclusion: The inflaton-gluon coupling can solve the axion isocurvature problem while enabling viable axion dark matter production, but only works for plateau-like inflationary potentials. The mechanism also opens up viable parameter space for models otherwise disfavored by CMB data by shifting the spectral index to bluer values.

title: Lyman-alpha Radiation Pressure in Dense Star Clusters: Implications for Star Formation and Winds at Cosmic Dawn
comment: 19 pages, 7 figures. Submitted to ApJ. Comments and suggestions welcome!
summary: Observations with the JWST in lensed fields have revealed that galaxies at cosmic dawn may concentrate their star formation in highly dense, compact, star clusters. The high columns and low metallicities encountered in their birth environments suggest that Lyman-alpha (Ly$α$) radiation pressure may be crucial to their formation and evolution. In this study, we address this question by post-processing snapshots from radiation hydrodynamic simulations of dense star cluster-forming clouds ($Σ_*\gtrsim10^3{M_\odot{pc}^{-2}}$) with a range of dust abundances ($Z_d=0-0.1Z_{d,\odot}$) using the COLT Monte Carlo code. We infer that Ly$α$ is likely to have mild (~10%) effects on the gas-to-star conversion efficiencies ($ε_*\gtrsim60$%) for $Z_d\gtrsim0.01Z_{d,\odot}$, and even in dust-free environments, $ε_*\gtrsim25$% - much higher than the <10% values typical of star-forming regions in the local Universe. This is because the densest filaments dominating stellar mass assembly ($n\gtrsim10^4{cm}^{-3}$) remain sub-Eddington ($f_{Edd}<1$). On the other hand, the bulk of the gas volume ($n\lesssim10^3{cm}^{-3}$) has $f_{Edd}>1$, with noticeable fractions having $f_{Edd}\gtrsim10$, implying that Ly$α$ can launch dynamically significant winds from these systems rapidly ($\lesssim$4Myr), with possible implications for ionizing photon escape and galactic outflows. The Ly$α$ force multiplier $M_F$ is highly sensitive to $Z_d$, with $M_F\lesssim3$ ($\lesssim 500$) for $0.1Z_{d,\odot}$ (dust-free) environments respectively. Nevertheless, Ly$α$ dominates over UV and IR radiation pressure at all values of $Z_d\lesssim0.1Z_{d,\odot}$, by factors of ~3-500. Our results suggest that Ly$α$ radiation pressure reinforces the emerging picture of locally efficient, bursty star formation accompanied by rapid outflows in galaxies at cosmic dawn.

AI.tldr: Using COLT Monte Carlo simulations post-processed from radiation hydrodynamic simulations, this study finds that Lyα radiation pressure has mild (~10%) effects on star formation efficiency in dense star clusters at cosmic dawn (ε*>60% for Zd≥0.01Z₀, ε*≥25% dust-free), but can launch rapid, dynamically significant winds (≤4 Myr) from low-density gas regions, dominating over UV/IR radiation pressure by factors of 3-500.
AI.motivation: JWST observations reveal that galaxies at cosmic dawn form stars in highly dense, compact clusters. The low metallicities and high gas columns in these environments suggest Lyα radiation pressure may be critical to their formation and evolution, yet its quantitative effects remain poorly understood.
AI.method: Post-processing snapshots from radiation hydrodynamic simulations of dense star cluster-forming clouds (Σ*≳10³ M⊙ pc⁻²) across a range of dust abundances (Zd=0–0.1 Z⊙) using the COLT Monte Carlo radiative transfer code, computing Eddington ratios, force multipliers, and star formation efficiencies.
AI.result: Lyα has mild (~10%) effects on gas-to-star conversion efficiency for Zd≳0.01 Z⊙ (ε*≳60%), and even in dust-free environments ε*≳25% (much higher than <10% in local Universe). Dense filaments (n≳10⁴ cm⁻³) remain sub-Eddington (fEdd<1), while bulk gas (n≲10³ cm⁻³) has fEdd>1 with fractions reaching fEdd≳10, enabling rapid winds (≤4 Myr). Lyα force multiplier MF ranges from <3 (0.1 Z⊙) to <500 (dust-free). Lyα dominates over UV and IR radiation pressure at all Zd≲0.1 Z⊙ by factors of ~3-500.
AI.conclusion: Lyα radiation pressure reinforces the emerging picture of locally efficient, bursty star formation accompanied by rapid outflows in galaxies at cosmic dawn, with implications for ionizing photon escape and galactic outflow driving.

title: Primordial Black Hole from Tensor-induced Density Fluctuation: First-order Phase Transitions and Domain Walls
comment: 24 pages, 12 figures, 3 tables+ appendices
summary: We present a novel \textit{gauge-invariant and minimal} formation mechanism of primordial black holes (PBHs) in first-order phase transition (FOPT) and domain walls (DW) separately. This is based on the first-order tensor perturbations, generated during FOPT from bubble collisions \& sound waves, and from DW annihilation, sourcing curvature, at second-order in perturbation theory. We show that the PBH formation implies \textit{model-independent constraints} on FOPT parameters ($β/H, α, T_{\star}$ ) and on DW parameters, ($α_{\rm ann}, V_{\rm bias}, σ$), from existing PBH constraints. We find that asteroid mass PBHs can become the entire dark matter (DM) of the Universe, for $T_{\star} \in (4 \times 10^{2}, 10^{4})$ GeV, for $β/H \simeq 6$, involving $α>\mathcal{O}(1)$ values. The corresponding FOPT Gravitational Waves (GW) amplitude will have its characteristic peak at $Ω_{\rm GW}^{\rm p} h^2$ $\sim \mathcal{O}(10^{-8})$ between frequencies $f_{\rm p} \in ({10^{-5},10^{-2}})$ Hz which is within the reach in LISA and SKA detectors. PBH as entire DM is possible for $σ^{1/3} \in [10^{6}, 10^{8}]$ TeV, for $V_{\rm bias}^{1/4} \in [10^7, 10^{10}]$ MeV with the corresponding GW amplitude peak from DW annihilation $Ω_{\rm GW}^{\rm p} h^2$ $\sim \mathcal{O}(10^{-9})$ (for $α_{\rm ann} \sim 10^{-2}$) and peak frequencies between $f_{\rm p} \in (4 \times {10^{-4},10^{-1}})$ Hz with ($T_{\rm ann} \in 4.5 \times [10^3, 10^6] $) GeV within the reach in LISA and ET detectors. We also provide semi-analytical formulae for the tensor-induced density spectrum, $P_{δ^{(2)}}$, $M_{\rm PBH}$ and $f_{\rm PBH}$, relating them in terms of FOPT and DW parameters which in turn, are related to viable particle physics origin of such FOPT and DW, and therefore, constrain such microphysics, either in the visible, or in dark sector models.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a gauge-invariant formation mechanism for primordial black holes (PBHs) from first-order phase transitions (FOPT) and domain walls (DW), deriving model-independent constraints on their parameters. It shows that asteroid-mass PBHs could constitute all dark matter, with detectable gravitational wave signals in LISA, SKA, and ET detectors.
AI.motivation: To establish a novel, gauge-invariant, and minimal mechanism for PBH formation from FOPT and DW, and derive model-independent constraints linking PBH abundance, dark matter, and gravitational wave signatures.
AI.method: The authors use first-order tensor perturbations generated during FOPT (from bubble collisions and sound waves) and DW annihilation, which source curvature perturbations at second order in perturbation theory. They derive semi-analytical formulae for the tensor-induced density spectrum, PBH mass, and abundance, relating them to FOPT parameters (β/H, α, T₍) and DW parameters (αₐₙₙ, V_bias, σ).
AI.result: Asteroid-mass PBHs can constitute the entire dark matter for T₍ ∈ (4×10², 10⁴) GeV with β/H ≃ 6 and α > O(1). For DW, PBH as all DM is possible for σ¹/³ ∈ [10⁶, 10⁸] TeV, V_bias¹/⁴ ∈ [10⁷, 10¹⁰] MeV. Corresponding GW peak amplitudes are Ω_GW^p h² ~ O(10⁻⁸) for FOPT (frequencies 10⁻⁵–10⁻² Hz, detectable by LISA/SKA) and ~ O(10⁻⁹) for DW (frequencies 4×10⁻⁴–10⁻¹ Hz, detectable by LISA/ET).
AI.conclusion: The formation mechanism provides model-independent constraints on both FOPT and DW parameters from existing PBH constraints, linking these to viable particle physics models in visible or dark sectors, and yielding testable GW signatures for future detectors.

title: Ionization Structure and Metal Enrichment of the Galactic Center Minispiral Observed with JWST
comment: Main text 13 pages, 10 figures, 5 Tables. Submitted to ApJ. Comments welcomed
summary: Sgr A* is the nearest quiescent supermassive black hole, and its proximity offers a unique opportunity to study its surrounding fuel supply. We leverage extensive spatial and spectroscopic information provided by the \jwst/MIRI MRS instrument to disentangle mid-infrared ionized gas structures in the central 0.1 parsec of the Galaxy. The Galactic Minispiral's Bar and Northern Arm are revealed by their distinct morphological and kinematic signatures. Several compact ($<1$\arcsec) gas structures including X7 also appear within $\sim 0.05$ parsec of Sgr A* in the plane of the sky, moving with blue-shifted radial velocities $\gtrsim 600$ km/s. Fine structure line measurements spanning ionization energies $\sim 7 - 55$ eV are used to constrain the incident radiation field, metal abundances (neon, argon, sulfur, nickel, and iron), and dust depletion/destruction for each identified gas structure. Overall, the Minispiral gas metallicity is $\sim 1-2.5~Z_\sun$, with a Wolf-Rayet star-driven ionizing radiation field, and significant nickel and iron dust destruction. Increased flux at energies $\gtrsim 41$ eV suggests that the compact gas structures experience an additional harder ionizing radiation source, which is most likely driven by localized fast radiative shocks from stellar winds, a hypothetical Sgr A* outflow, and/or interactions with the ambient medium.

AI.tldr: Using JWST/MIRI MRS, this paper analyzes ionized gas structures within 0.1 pc of Sgr A*, revealing the Minispiral's Bar and Northern Arm, compact blue-shifted gas features near the black hole, and constrains metallicity (~1-2.5 Z☉), radiation sources (Wolf-Rayet stars and harder ionizing source), and dust destruction.
AI.motivation: To leverage JWST's high spatial/spectral resolution to study the fuel supply and gas dynamics in the immediate vicinity of the nearest quiescent supermassive black hole, Sgr A*.
AI.method: JWST/MIRI MRS mid-infrared spectroscopic imaging to map ionized gas structures, measure fine-structure emission lines (ionization energies 7–55 eV), and derive radiation field, metallicity, and dust depletion parameters for each identified structure.
AI.result: The Minispiral (Bar and Northern Arm) shows distinct morphological/kinematic signatures; compact structures (e.g., X7) within ~0.05 pc of Sgr A* exhibit blue-shifted velocities ≥600 km/s; gas metallicity is 1–2.5 Z☉ with a Wolf-Rayet-driven radiation field; significant Ni and Fe dust destruction is found; excess flux at ≥41 eV indicates an additional harder ionizing source likely from fast radiative shocks.
AI.conclusion: The Galactic center's ionized gas is shaped by multiple radiation sources, with Wolf-Rayet stars dominating the Minispiral and compact gas structures requiring an additional hard ionizing component (stellar wind shocks, Sgr A* outflow, or ambient interactions), providing new constraints on the black hole's fuel supply.

title: Constraining the Galactic Center Dark Cluster with ELT/MICADO Observations
comment: Accepted for publication in A&A (aa59043-26)
summary: The Galactic Center hosts the densest known stellar environment in the Milky Way, dominated by the massive black hole Sgr A* and the surrounding nuclear star cluster. Theory predicts that this region should also contain a large population of stellar compact objects (SCOs) - black holes, neutron stars, and white dwarfs - forming a "dark cluster" whose distribution and properties remain observationally unconstrained. These unseen stellar remnants are central to questions of mass segregation, cluster dynamics, and the expected rate of extreme mass ratio inspirals (EMRIs) detectable by future gravitational-wave observatories including LISA. Current evidence for SCOs in the Galactic Center is indirect, relying on dynamical mass measurements, X-ray surveys, and a small number of transient sources. Direct detections remain elusive due to crowding, extinction, and the sensitivity limits of existing instruments. We explore how upcoming facilities, in particular the Extremely Large Telescope (ELT) with its first-light imager MICADO, can fundamentally transform this field. MICADO's combination of deep photometry, high spatial resolution, and precise astrometry will enable systematic searches for SCO-star binaries via photometric variability and orbital astrometric signatures, as well as direct detection of isolated accreting black holes interacting with the gas-rich Galactic Center environment. We outline the observational pathways, technical challenges, and expected sensitivities, showing that ELT/MICADO observations can provide the first quantitative constraints on the dark cluster population. Establishing these constraints will be pivotal for understanding the dynamical evolution of the Galactic Center, the role of compact remnants in nuclear star clusters, and the astrophysical context of gravitational-wave sources in galactic nuclei.

AI.tldr: The paper explores how ELT/MICADO will enable the first direct observational constraints on the hidden population of stellar compact objects (black holes, neutron stars, white dwarfs) in the Galactic Center, addressing key gaps in our understanding of the "dark cluster" dynamics, mass segregation, and EMRI rates for LISA.
AI.motivation: The Galactic Center's "dark cluster" of stellar compact objects (SCOs) is observationally unconstrained, yet crucial for understanding mass segregation, cluster dynamics, and EMRI rates detectable by LISA. Current evidence is indirect and limited, motivating the need for transformative observational capabilities.
AI.method: The study outlines observational pathways using ELT/MICADO (deep photometry, high spatial resolution, precise astrometry) for systematic searches of SCO-star binaries via photometric variability and astrometric signatures, and direct detection of isolated accreting BHs in the gas-rich environment.
AI.result: ELT/MICADO observations can provide the first quantitative constraints on the dark cluster population, overcoming current limitations due to crowding, extinction, and instrument sensitivity.
AI.conclusion: Establishing these constraints is pivotal for understanding the dynamical evolution of the Galactic Center, the role of compact remnants in nuclear star clusters, and the astrophysical context of gravitational-wave sources in galactic nuclei.

title: Reconstructing the Stripping History of the Sagittarius Stream with Neural Networks
comment: 14 pages, 5 figures, accepted for Publication in ApJ
summary: The Sagittarius (Sgr) Stream is produced by the ongoing disruption of the Sgr dwarf spheroidal (dSph) galaxy and is thought to contain multiple wraps that were stripped during different pericentric passages. In this study, we introduce a neural-network--based method trained on $N$-body simulations to infer the stripping time of Sgr Stream stars directly from their phase-space coordinates. We combine spectroscopic data from SEGUE, APOGEE DR17, and LAMOST DR7 LRS with \textit{Gaia} EDR3 astrometry and distance estimates from the latest \texttt{StarHorse} catalog to identify high-quality Sgr Stream members. Applying our method to these stars, we measure a clear metallicity gradient with stripping time, well described by a linear relation with slope $\sim 0.3~\mathrm{dex~Gyr^{-1}}$. We further predict the stripping times of globular clusters previously suggested to originate from the Sgr dSph. M 54, Terzan 7, Terzan 8, and Arp 2 exhibit stripping times consistent with being currently bound to the Sgr remnant. Pal 12, Whiting 1, and NGC 2419 are inferred to have been stripped $0.9 \pm 0.1$, $1.1 \pm 0.2$, and $2.1 \pm 0.2$ Gyr ago, respectively. For NGC 4147 and NGC 5634, whose membership in the Sgr system remains uncertain, our analysis suggests stripping times of $1.1 \pm 0.4$ and $1.1 \pm 0.1$ Gyr, respectively, if they are ultimately confirmed as genuine Sgr members. These results demonstrate that data-driven models of dynamical stripping histories offer a promising approach for reconstructing the formation and chemical evolution of the Sgr Stream.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces a neural-network method trained on N-body simulations to infer the stripping time of Sagittarius Stream stars from phase-space coordinates. Using spectroscopic and astrometric data, they find a metallicity gradient of ~0.3 dex/Gyr with stripping time, and predict stripping times for several globular clusters associated with the Sgr dSph galaxy.
AI.motivation: To understand the dynamical disruption history of the Sagittarius dwarf spheroidal galaxy by inferring when stars were stripped from it, and to reconstruct the formation and chemical evolution of the Sgr Stream.
AI.method: A neural-network-based method trained on N-body simulations to infer stripping time directly from phase-space coordinates, applied to Sgr Stream member stars identified from SEGUE, APOGEE DR17, LAMOST DR7 LRS, Gaia EDR3 astrometry, and StarHorse distances.
AI.result: A clear metallicity gradient of ~0.3 dex/Gyr with stripping time is measured. Stripping times are inferred for globular clusters: M54, Terzan 7, Terzan 8, Arp 2 are bound to the Sgr remnant; Pal 12 (~0.9 Gyr ago), Whiting 1 (~1.1 Gyr), NGC 2419 (~2.1 Gyr) were stripped; NGC 4147 and NGC 5634 have estimated stripping times of ~1.1 Gyr if confirmed as Sgr members.
AI.conclusion: Data-driven models of dynamical stripping histories are a promising approach for reconstructing the formation and chemical evolution of the Sgr Stream.

title: An Updated Characterization of Luminous Lyα emitters at the End of Reionization
comment: 14 pages, 5 figures, submitted to ApJL, comments welcome
summary: We present a multi-wavelength physical characterization of 14 luminous Ly$α$ emitters (LAEs) at $z\approx6$, integrating deep ground-based Magellan/M2FS spectroscopy with heterogeneous JWST/NIRCam broad- and medium-band imaging. Identified via strong Ly$α$ lines with extreme Ly$α$ luminosities of ${>}10^{42.6}$ erg s$^{-1}$, the sample exhibits very large rest-frame equivalent widths (${\gtrsim}100$ Å) and steeply blue UV continua ($β_{\rm median}\simeq-2.2$, $-18.2>M_{\rm 1500}>-20.2$ mag). Crucially, the integration of NIRCam medium-band photometry (F410M) breaks the degeneracy between strong rest-optical nebular emission and Balmer breaks, resolving prior mass overestimations. The tightly constrained spectral energy distribution modeling demonstrates that these luminous LAEs tend to be unequivocally low-mass, ultra-young dwarf starbursts; half the sample is characterized by stellar masses of $M_* < 10^8 M_{\odot}$, ages $\lesssim10$ Myr, and negligible dust attenuation. We also map the production efficiency of ionizing photons and Ly$α$ escape fractions ($f_{\rm esc}^{\rm Lyα}$). The $f_{\rm esc}^{\rm Lyα}$ values are exceptionally high, with a median of ${\gtrsim}40$%, increasing for the bluer UV continua. Finally, analyzing spatial offsets between the Ly$α$ centroid and the stellar counterpart, we demonstrate empirically that internal dust content, rather than neutral hydrogen gas, dominate the suppression of Ly$α$ radiative transfer. Our study reveals that strong Ly$α$ emission of the luminous LAEs are generally attributed to both the vigorous starburst activities and the high $f_{\rm esc}^{\rm Lyα}$. Resembling Lyman continuum leakers, these extreme dwarf systems function as highly efficient ionizing engines at the conclusion of the Epoch of Reionization.

AI.tldr: This paper characterizes 14 luminous Lyα emitters at z≈6 using Magellan/M2FS spectroscopy and JWST/NIRCam imaging. NIRCam medium-band photometry resolves prior mass overestimations, showing these are ultra-young, low-mass dwarf starbursts (half with M* < 10⁸ M⊙, ages <10 Myr). They exhibit extremely high Lyα escape fractions (median >40%) and efficient ionizing photon production, resembling Lyman continuum leakers that powered reionization.
AI.motivation: To resolve degeneracies in spectral energy distribution modeling of high-z LAEs (particularly between nebular emission and Balmer breaks) and accurately characterize the physical properties of luminous Lyα emitters at the epoch of reionization.
AI.method: Multi-wavelength analysis combining deep Magellan/M2FS spectroscopy (for Lyα lines) with heterogeneous JWST/NIRCam broad- and medium-band imaging (especially F410M to break the nebular emission vs. Balmer break degeneracy), plus SED modeling and spatial offset analysis.
AI.result: Luminous LAEs are ultra-young, low-mass dwarf starbursts (M* < 10⁸ M⊙, ages <10 Myr, negligible dust). Lyα escape fractions are exceptionally high (median >40%). Internal dust dominates Lyα suppression over neutral hydrogen. These systems are efficient ionizing engines resembling Lyman continuum leakers.
AI.conclusion: Strong Lyα emission in luminous LAEs arises from both vigorous starburst activity and high Lyα escape fractions, establishing these extreme dwarf systems as highly efficient ionizing engines at the end of the Epoch of Reionization.

title: Observation of spontaneous N-bearing PAH formation using ion trap: a new formation pathway in the interstellar medium
summary: Nitrogen-bearing polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (N-PAHs) are key precursors to complex organic molecules in both the interstellar medium and the nitrogen-rich planetary atmospheres. Despite the recent detections of nitrogen-functionalized astromolecules, their formation pathways remain an open question. The discrepancies between their predicted and observed abundances point to unknown mechanism that govern their evolution in the astrophysical environments. Employing an ion trap technique and electronic structure calculations, we unravel multiple barrier-less reactions between gas-phase pyrimidine cations (C$_4$H$_4$N$_2^+$) and acetylene (C$_2$H$_2$) which form an hitherto unreported endocyclic- N-PAHs (C$_8$H$_7$N$_2^+$). The present measurements on reactions involving a double-nitrogen subsituted aromatic heterocycle have implications to the astrochemistry of both the Titan's atmosphere and interstellar medium.

AI.tldr: This study reveals barrier-less reactions between pyrimidine cations and acetylene forming endocyclic N-PAHs (C₈H₇N₂⁺), providing a new formation pathway for nitrogen-bearing complex molecules in interstellar and planetary environments.
AI.motivation: The discrepancies between predicted and observed abundances of nitrogen-functionalized astromolecules point to unknown formation mechanisms governing their evolution in astrophysical environments.
AI.method: Ion trap technique combined with electronic structure calculations.
AI.result: Multiple barrier-less reactions between gas-phase pyrimidine cations (C₄H₄N₂⁺) and acetylene (C₂H₂) forming previously unreported endocyclic N-PAHs (C₈H₇N₂⁺).
AI.conclusion: These findings on double-nitrogen substituted aromatic heterocycle reactions have implications for astrochemistry in both Titan's atmosphere and the interstellar medium.

title: Discovery of a Compact Hub-Filament System in G286.21+0.17 with JWST and ALMA: Insights into Protocluster Formation and Competitive Accretion
summary: We present a multi-wavelength study of the massive protocluster G286.21+0.17 (G286) using \emph{JWST} near-infrared imaging and ALMA H$^{13}$CO$^{+}$(1--0) observations. The \emph{JWST} images uncover a compact ($\sim$0.5 pc) hub-filament system (HFS), comprising a dense central hub connected by at least four converging filaments seen in absorption, along with multiple H$_2$ protostellar jets/outflows. The hub hosts dense core G286c1. The H$^{13}$CO$^{+}$ emission confirms this HFS over [$-$19.2, $-$16.4]~km~s$^{-1}$. The \emph{JWST} images further trace prominent photodissociation regions around the H\,{\sc ii}~region~A, powered by a B-type star. The radial distribution of ALMAGAL 1.38 mm core properties reveals steep power-law slopes toward the hub center. Within the inner hub (r < 8'', $\sim0.1$~pc), the core number density follows $ρ~[\rm pc^{-2}] \propto r^{-2.4\pm0.5}$, the surface density scales as $Σ~[\rm g~cm^{-2}] \propto r^{-1.0\pm0.2}$, and the enclosed core mass varies as $M_{\rm core}~[M_{\odot}] \propto r^{-1.2\pm0.2}$, while core diameters remain approximately constant ($D_{\rm core}~[\rm AU] \propto r^{-0.1\pm0.1}$). These trends, along with filament mass accretion rates of $7\times10^{-6}$--$1.8\times10^{-4}$~$M_\odot$~yr$^{-1}$, support a competitive accretion scenario in which gravitational focusing enhances core growth toward the hub center. Filament linewidths increase from tail/outer-region to head/hub-region, consistent with gravity-driven turbulence. However, the absence of a preferred alignment between velocity gradients and gravitational force directions may indicate a dynamically evolved system. The HFS likely formed through large-scale gas layer interactions and compression by the adjacent H\,{\sc ii} region. Overall, star formation in G286 appears regulated by filamentary accretion, competitive core growth in the hub, and stellar feedback.

AI.tldr: JWST near-infrared imaging and ALMA H¹³CO⁺ observations reveal a compact hub-filament system in the massive protocluster G286.21+0.17, with filamentary accretion, competitive core growth toward the hub center, and stellar feedback shaping star formation.
AI.motivation: To understand the physical processes governing massive star and cluster formation, specifically how hub-filament systems (HFS) accumulate mass, form cores, and respond to stellar feedback in a massive protocluster environment.
AI.method: Multi-wavelength study combining JWST near-infrared imaging (tracing absorption structures, H₂ jets/outflows, and PDRs) with ALMA H¹³CO⁺ line observations (tracing the 3D gas kinematics). Radial distributions of ALMAGAL 1.38 mm core properties were analyzed and power-law slopes fitted.
AI.result: A compact (~0.5 pc) hub-filament system with four converging filaments was identified. Core properties show steep power-law gradients toward the hub: number density ∝ r⁻²·⁴, surface density ∝ r⁻¹·⁰, enclosed mass ∝ r⁻¹·², while core diameter is nearly constant (∝ r⁻⁰·¹). Filament mass accretion rates of 7×10⁻⁶–1.8×10⁻⁴ M⊙ yr⁻¹ were measured. Filament linewidths increase from tail to hub, but velocity gradients lack preferential alignment with gravitational forces.
AI.conclusion: Star formation in G286 is regulated by three key mechanisms: filamentary accretion feeding the hub, competitive accretion (gravitational focusing) enhancing core growth toward the center, and stellar feedback from the adjacent H II region. The HFS likely formed via large-scale gas layer interactions and H II region compression. The misaligned velocity gradients suggest a dynamically evolved system rather than one in simple gravitational collapse.

title: Boundary-supported radial layering in Hoag-like ring galaxies
comment: 5 pages, 3 figures; submitted to MNRAS Letters
summary: Clean Hoag-like ring galaxies are often characterized by an old compact central component, a depleted gap, and a detached outer ring. We identify a boundary-supported radial-layering mechanism in a shell-deformed Kepler control model. A compact inner boundary supplies the core state, while a localized effective shell deformation, interpreted as the reduced imprint of externally supplied material settled near a finite circularization radius, needs to create only an internal maximum and a subsequent outer minimum. These act as the gap barrier and ring-supporting well. The onset of this structure is organized by a saddle-node threshold of the critical-point equation. In a 10^4-point Monte Carlo scan, shell-localized boundary-supported candidates occupy finite parameter volume under the adopted priors, and none of the localized candidates contains an ordered interior minimum--maximum--minimum subsequence. The same branch gives a scale-free gap-to-ring interval overlapping representative ratios for Hoag's Object, UGC 4599, and PGC 1000714, but not for the environmentally processed comparison object JO171.

AI.tldr: The paper identifies a boundary-supported radial-layering mechanism in a shell-deformed Kepler model to explain the structure of Hoag-like ring galaxies (compact core, depleted gap, outer ring). The mechanism relies on a saddle-node threshold, and Monte Carlo simulations show it reproduces gap-to-ring intervals for Hoag's Object, UGC 4599, and PGC 1000714, but not for JO171.
AI.motivation: To explain the formation mechanism of clean Hoag-like ring galaxies, which feature an old compact core, a depleted gap, and a detached outer ring, through a dynamical model rather than environmental or tidal interactions.
AI.method: A shell-deformed Kepler control model is used, where a compact inner boundary provides the core state and a localized shell deformation (interpreted as accreted material at a finite circularization radius) creates an internal maximum and outer minimum in the radial profile, forming the gap barrier and ring-supporting well. The onset is organized by a saddle-node threshold of the critical-point equation. A 10,000-point Monte Carlo scan is conducted to test the parameter space.
AI.result: Shell-localized boundary-supported candidates occupy finite parameter volume under adopted priors; none contain an ordered interior minimum-maximum-minimum subsequence. The model yields a scale-free gap-to-ring interval that matches observed ratios for Hoag's Object, UGC 4599, and PGC 1000714, but fails to match the environmentally processed comparison object JO171.
AI.conclusion: The proposed boundary-supported radial-layering mechanism successfully reproduces the structural properties of clean Hoag-like ring galaxies, distinguishing them from environmentally processed systems like JO171.

title: DREAMS. JWST Spectroscopy of a $z=8.3$ Galaxy with an ALMA Dust Continuum Detection: Early Dust, Very High $T_{\rm dust}$, and a Multi-wavelength [OIII] Ratio Discrepancy
comment: 18 pages, 18 figure, Submitted to ApJ
summary: We present a deep DREAMS JWST/NIRSpec MSA medium-grating spectrum of MACS0416-Y1, a galaxy at $z=8.312$ with the highest-redshift ALMA dust continuum detection to date, in order to characterize its properties together with archival IFU and ALMA data. The deep NIRSpec spectrum reveals a broad H$β$ line with a width of $\sim1100$ km s$^{-1}$. We interpret it as a broad-line AGN whose line diagnostics are consistent with AGN activity across its clumpy structure, given the absence of little red dot signatures. MACS0416-Y1 clearly shows [OIII]4363 emission, suggesting a moderately low metallicity of $12+\log(\mathrm{O/H})=7.86^{+0.09}_{-0.08}$ ($0.15~Z_\odot$). The combination of [CII]158$μ$m and dust continuum emission indicates low dust mass ratios of $\log (M_{\rm dust}/M_{\rm gas})=-3.60^{+0.29}_{-0.22}$ and $\log (M_{\rm dust}/M_{\rm metal})=-0.95^{+0.29}_{-0.20}$. Because the metallicity of MACS0416-Y1 is around the critical metallicity of $0.1\textrm{-}0.2~Z_\odot$, the system is expected to undergo dust growth, explaining these low dust mass ratios as well as its small dust mass, $M_{\rm dust}\sim10^6~M_\odot$. The intense UV radiation from the AGN may contribute to a high dust temperature of $T_{\rm dust}\simeq 91^{+62}_{-35}$ K, boosting the dust-continuum emission above the ALMA detection limit despite the small $M_{\rm dust}$ at $z>8$. We find a very high total flux ratio of [OIII]88$μ$m/[OIII]5007 = $0.26 \pm 0.06$ in MACS0416-Y1, above predictions from single ionized nebular models at any electron density. This discrepancy suggests that the [OIII]88$μ$m and [OIII]5007 trace largely distinct regions, with the optical line suppressed in dusty nebulae, and thus requires careful interpretation when combining optical and infrared emission lines in JWST+ALMA studies.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes JWST/NIRSpec and ALMA data of MACS0416-Y1 (z=8.312), finding a broad Hβ line from an AGN, low metallicity (0.15 Z⊙), low dust/gas and dust/metal mass ratios, high dust temperature (~91 K), and an unusually high [OIII]88μm/[OIII]5007 flux ratio suggesting distinct emission regions probed by optical vs. infrared lines.
AI.motivation: To characterize the properties of MACS0416-Y1, the highest-redshift galaxy with ALMA dust continuum detection, using deep JWST/NIRSpec spectroscopy combined with archival IFU and ALMA data.
AI.method: Deep JWST/NIRSpec MSA medium-grating spectroscopy of MACS0416-Y1 at z=8.312, complemented by archival IFU and ALMA data; analysis of emission line diagnostics (broad Hβ, [OIII]4363, [OIII]88μm, [OIII]5007), dust continuum, and [CII]158μm to derive metallicity, dust masses, gas masses, and dust temperature.
AI.result: Broad Hβ line (~1100 km/s) indicating an AGN; metallicity 12+log(O/H)=7.86 (0.15 Z⊙); low dust mass ratios (log(Mdust/Mgas)=-3.60, log(Mdust/Mmetal)=-0.95); small dust mass ~10⁶ M⊙; high dust temperature ~91 K; high [OIII]88μm/[OIII]5007 flux ratio (0.26±0.06) exceeding single-ionized nebular model predictions.
AI.conclusion: MACS0416-Y1 hosts an AGN with metallicity near the critical threshold (0.1-0.2 Z⊙) for dust growth, explaining its low dust masses; AGN UV radiation may heat dust to high temperatures, making it detectable despite low mass; the high [OIII] line ratio indicates optical and infrared lines trace distinct ionized regions, requiring careful multi-wavelength interpretation.

title: Identifying group galaxies merging with massive clusters using machine learning
comment: Accepted for publication in MNRAS. 18 pages, 17 figures
summary: The environment plays a critical role in galaxy evolution, with galaxy clusters and their infall regions offering diverse conditions that shape galaxies before they enter the dense cluster core, a process known as ``pre-processing''. However, identifying environmental substructures, particularly galaxy groups in these transitional zones, remains challenging due to projection effects and ``fingers-of-god'' distortions. In this work, we present a supervised machine learning framework for classifying galaxies into three environmental categories: main cluster, group, and neither, using observable galaxy properties such as positions, line-of-sight velocities, and stellar mass. The model is trained on mock observations derived from cosmological simulations designed to replicate survey conditions and achieves an overall accuracy and class-size-weighted precision of 81%. The neither and main cluster populations are reliably recovered, whereas group galaxies remain the most challenging to identify, achieving 30% completeness and 76% purity. Within $1\times R_{200}$, classification performance is suppressed, but it improves beyond this radius, reaching 40% completeness and 80% purity. Resampling and thresholding strategies allow the model to be tuned toward either higher purity or higher completeness; in this study, we adopt first-past-the-post thresholding to emphasise purity. Model performance is consistent across cluster masses and dynamical states, and it outperforms both Friends-of-Friends and Gaussian Mixture Modelling. This flexibility makes it well suited to upcoming spectroscopic surveys of cluster infall regions, providing a robust statistical tool for disentangling environmental influences on galaxy evolution.

AI.tldr: A supervised machine learning framework classifies galaxies into main cluster, group, and neither categories using observable properties (positions, velocities, stellar mass), achieving 81% accuracy and outperforming traditional methods like Friends-of-Friends and Gaussian Mixture Modelling. Group galaxies remain the most challenging to identify (30% completeness, 76% purity), but the method provides a robust statistical tool for studying galaxy pre-processing in cluster infall regions.
